title: Recursion Announces Alignment with FDA on Registrational Phase 3 Trial Design for REC-4881 in Familial Adenomatous Polyposis
content: Recursion Announces Alignment with FDA on Registrational Phase 3 Trial Design for REC-4881 in Familial Adenomatous Polyposis November 18, 2026 at 4:59 AM EST PDF Version REC-4881 is among the first AI-enabled programs to advance a registrational Phase 3 trial design for a disease with no approved pharmacologic therapies. Its potential as a first-in-class oral therapy for FAP was identified through unbiased phenotypic screening using Recursion’s AI foundation models. Achieved a key regulatory milestone with FDA alignment on including excision of adenomas ≥10 mm throughout the GI as a novel and clinically meaningful event in the composite event-free survival primary endpoint. Adenomas of this size are associated with an increased risk of high-grade dysplasia, and cancer. Modified Spigelman stage progression and total polyp burden will be included among secondary endpoints. The trial is expected to enroll approximately 200 adults with FAP following colectomy or proctocolectomy and is on track to begin in the second half of 2027. Salt Lake City, UT , Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Recursion (Nasdaq: RXRX), a leading clinical-stage company pioneering AI-enabled drug discovery and development, today announced that it has aligned with the FDA on the design of its registrational Phase 3 trial of REC-4881, an investigational oral MEK1/2 inhibitor for the treatment of familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP). The alignment includes a composite event-free survival primary endpoint with a novel, clinically meaningful component: excision of an adenoma 10 mm or larger in either the upper or lower gastrointestinal (GI) tract. The trial is on track to begin in the second half of 2027. REC-4881 is among the first AI-enabled programs to advance a registrational Phase 3 trial design for a disease with no approved pharmacologic therapies. Its potential as a first-in-class oral therapy for FAP was identified through unbiased phenotypic screening using Recursion’s AI foundation models. "Adenomas 10 millimeters and larger are associated with increased cancer risk and are nowadays routinely removed in patients with FAP. However, removal carries risks of bleeding and perforation, alongside the burden of repeated procedures and intensive surveillance," said Dr. Evelien Dekker , Head of Expert Clinic for Familial and Hereditary Polyposis and Colorectal Cancer, and Professor of Gastrointestinal Oncology, Amsterdam University Medical Center . “There is a substantial unmet need for a therapy that could prevent adenomas from reaching this size or developing in cancer. Reducing the need for these interventions could provide a meaningful benefit to patients." “Patients with familial adenomatous polyposis face a lifelong burden of endoscopic surveillance, repeated interventions, and frequently major surgery. A medical therapy that could safely and durably prevent the progression of adenomas, reduce the need for endoscopic interventions, and potentially delay or avoid major surgery would represent a significant advance in the management of FAP,” said Dr. Robert Hüneburg, MD, Senior Gastroenterologist and Head of the Hereditary Tumor Clinic , National Center for Hereditary Tumor Syndromes , Department of Internal Medicine I , University Hospital Bonn, Germany . “For people living with FAP, colectomy does not end the disease. Patients continue to face decades of lifelong surveillance, repeated polyp removal and, for some, further major surgery,” said Najat Khan , Ph.D., President and Chief Executive Officer of Recursion. “Our Phase 2 TUPELO results showed substantial and rapid reductions in polyp burden across the GI tract, including larger, higher-risk polyps, supporting our advancement toward a registrational trial. Securing FDA alignment on a novel component of our primary endpoint - counting the removal of adenomas 10 mm or larger across both the upper and lower GI tract as events - is a key milestone, reflecting an important and clinically meaningful intervention in FAP care. We appreciate the FDA’s constructive engagement and look forward to starting the trial in the second half of 2027, with the goal of bringing a much-needed treatment option to people living with FAP.” About the Phase 3 registrational trial The registrational Phase 3 trial is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven study expected to enroll approximately 200 patients with FAP aged 18 and older who have had a colectomy or proctocolectomy. The trial will evaluate REC-4881 at a dose of 4 mg, with the dosing schedule that will be determined based on data emerging from the ongoing TUPELO trial. Patients in both arms will be monitored with comprehensive endoscopic surveillance.
